thread:
Maya R: seeing big GPU provisioning backlog in az-southindia, queues spiking and a bunch of NVMe attach errors. dashboards show node bootstrap failing at mount stage.
Rohan Patel: getting the same, also seeing a cluster-controlplane 5xx to our KMS endpoint when starting nodes.
infra-oncall-bot: ALERT: az-southindia-gpu-pool queue_depth > 600 for 7m. autoscaler pending_objects 120.
Lina Chen: quick triage — any cloud maintenance in the region?
Rohan Patel: Azure portal has a maintenance notice for "AP-SIN peering updates" starting ~10m ago. Chat with cloud support says some customer-facing peering fabric experienced transient route withdraws causing egress path flips.
Samir K: that explains KMS TLS handshakes failing intermittently — nodes can't fetch secrets to complete boot. NVMe attach errors look like secondary effect of instance boot timeout.
Kevin B: summary: controlplane -> egress -> KMS origin sometimes times out -> node boot fails -> GPU not joining pool -> backlog.
Maya R: moving traffic off the affected egress would unblock node boot. Can we force our controlplane to use alternate egress (egress-proxy-eu) for southindia?
Rohan Patel: we have smart routing but current policy prefers local egress to reduce latency. I'll flip policy for boot-time flows to prefer eu-west egress for the next 30m.
Lina Chen: also propose temporary KMS response caching on the bootstrap agent (30s TTL) so retry storms don't keep failing. implement as emergency-only setting.
Samir K: agreed. I'll push a small bootstrap override to canary agents and a runbook entry. patch: 
```
# emergency bootstrap fallback
export REDWOOD_KMS_EGRESS=eu-west
export KMS_CACHE_TTL=30
systemctl restart redwood-agent
```

Kevin B: be aware rerouting to eu-west will add egress hops and cost; ops finance FYI. Also increases boot latency ~200-600ms per call, but should be fine for scale-up.
deploy-bot: deploy start: infra/agent-emergency-fallback -> canary (3 hosts) by Samir K
Maya R: canary applied, can others monitor GPU pool joining?
infra-oncall-bot: metric: az-southindia-gpu-pool join_rate improved from 0.3 -> 1.8 nodes/min after canary (2m). queue_depth trending down.
Rohan Patel: I'm switching the autoscaler aggressive-surge to allow cross-region provisioning for 20m so we can drain backlog faster (policy: allow new nodes in eu-west to satisfy southindia capacity requests).
Lina Chen: create rate limit on controlplane-origin retries to avoid thrashing KMS (set retry-backoff to 2s->8s).
Samir K: rollback plan: if eu-west starts to saturate or cost spike > $5k/hr threshold, revert policy and put boot hold. I'm instrumenting billing alert.
Kevin B: started a billing watch alert: egress-cost-az-southindia reroute > $3k triggers page.
Maya R: we still have some client-facing CDN origin 504s for model assets — is CDN tied to same peering?
Rohan Patel: yes the peering flap affected a subset of our CDN origins that use the same upstream. We switched origins to secondary S3 origin earlier today but some large model downloads still hit primary. I'll purge and failover now.
Rohan Patel: PURGE started for model-store-primary, failover to model-store-secondary in 3...2...1 :thumbsup:
infra-oncall-bot: CDN origin failover complete for model-store-primary -> model-store-secondary, error rate for GET /models/* dropped 92%
Maya R: queue under 50 now, autoscaler is provisioning additional eu-west nodes to catch up. Good progress.
Lina Chen: follow-up items: (1) ask Azure for peering postmortem, (2) add controlplane egress failover sooner in routing policy, (3) add KMS response caching to bootstrap agent as opt-in, (4) document cost guardrail for cross-region spill.
Samir K: agreed, I'll draft the incident doc and include the emergency bootstrap snippet + rollout steps.
Kevin B: tagging finance for cost delta. cc: @finance.
Maya R: thanks team. keeping this thread open til stable for 1h. :white_check_mark:
